sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Konstanz, on Lake Constance next to the Swiss border, has far more cars trying to reach its old town than the streets can hold, and the city steers them by fees and by hand. On 16 December 2025 the council decided to raise the on-street fee in the old town on the left of the Rhine to 3.00 euros an hour, Strandbad Horn to 2.50 euros and Strandbad Klausenhorn to 2.00 euros, with the aim that car parks are the cheaper choice for long stays and street spaces serve short stays; the city's May 2026 report says the higher rate applies from May 2026 [0]. An earlier proposal to raise the old-town rate from 2.00 to 3.00 euros was rejected on 29 April 2025 by 20 votes to 20 [1]. The resident permit costs 150 euros a year [3]. A draft Climate Mobility Plan presented in June 2026 would extend parking management and raise resident fees step by step to 600 euros a year and visitor fees to 6 euros an hour; it is a proposal, three parties oppose it according to one local outlet, and each measure needs its own council decision [4]. A scheme for Petershausen with 1,110 public spaces in three kinds of zone was due to start charging on 1 April 2026 [2]. Manual traffic management on about 60 high-load days a year closes and reopens access roads depending on how full the car parks are, and drivers are pointed to car parks on the right of the Rhine [6]. The rebuilt Bahnhofplatz, completed in October 2025, is closed to car traffic with exceptions for buses, bicycles, deliveries and exempted residents, and a digital traffic management system is to follow in the medium term [7]. The measure to halve the roughly 2,700 inner-city street spaces is marked as not begun, and the report notes that the number of resident permits is about double the supply of spaces [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Europabrücke car park, a mobility hub next to the long-distance bus station, went into operation in July 2025, cost about 18 million euros including land, and has about 740 to 750 spaces and 80 to 90 charge points according to different passages [13]. It was still used too little on Saturdays in late 2025, because its fee carries no bus ticket, and its busiest day was 2 May 2026 with 790 parking events and 493 cars at the peak; a Wasserbus boat to the harbour has run since April 2026 [16]. The Augustiner garage, with 288 spaces, has been closed since 1 March 2026 for a refurbishment of about 9 million euros, expected until about the end of 2026, and passes to the Stadtwerke group [14]. At the Döbele, the city plans to build over the car park with housing and move its parking into a mobility house of about 500 spaces, with no date given [15]. The Stephansplatz car park, with 78 spaces, is to cease, while 82 new spaces appeared at the Döbele [5]. Stadtwerke Konstanz Mobil operates 185 public charge points at 34 sites, 112 of them commissioned in 2025 [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The city's car park pages list seven car parks: Altstadt 359 spaces, LAGO 931, Marktstätte 277, Fischmarkt 161, Döbele 435, Europabrücke 745 and P+R Seepark 209. They are run by private companies, the city itself at the Döbele and the Stadtwerke at the Europabrücke [8]. The LAGO charges 3.00 euros an hour up to five hours with a maximum of 30 euros per 24 hours [9]. The Döbele charges 4.00 euros for up to one hour, 7.00 for two hours and 3.00 euros per further hour, with a maximum of 25 euros a day [11]. The Europabrücke charges 1.50 euros an hour in zone A and 1.00 euro in the other zones, with a monthly permit of 50 euros [10].

Our data cover six car parks. Altstadt (359 spaces) is the fullest, averaging 71% on weekdays and 62% at weekends over 52 days, and it reached full in single readings around midday on Saturdays. Döbele (435), Marktstätte (288 in our feed, against 277 on the city's page) and Fischmarkt (161) average about 50% to 54% every day, and LAGO (931) 24% on weekdays and 30% at weekends. The Europabrücke (745), measured only since 26 September, averaged 7% on weekdays and 5% at weekends, which matches the city's own statement that it is little used on ordinary days. The Augustiner garage is closed and has no readings.
